bibl.title: Two-Dimensional Gas of Massless Dirac Fermions in Graphene

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: existence
span.quote: Here we report a condensed matter system where electron transport is essentially governed by the Dirac equation and charge carriers mimic relativistic particles with zero mass and an effective “speed of light” c∗ ≈106m/s.

span.label: massless Dirac fermion transport in graphene
span.quote: Our studies of graphene – a single atomic layer of carbon – have revealed a variety of unusual phenomena characteristic of two-dimensional (2D) Dirac fermions.

span.label: laboratory-experiment
span.quote: To obtain graphene samples, we used the original procedures described in [1], which involve micromechanical cleavage of graphite followed by identification and selection of monolayers using a combination of optical, scanning-electron and atomic-force microscopies.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: in graphene the honeycomb lattice makes charge carriers behave as massless Dirac fermions obeying the relativistic Dirac equation rather than the Schrodinger equation
span.quote: revealed a variety of unusual phenomena characteristic of two-dimensional (2D) Dirac fermions

span.label: Carrier mobility in the devices is probably still limited by defects inherited from the parent graphite, so the measured mobility is not intrinsic.
span.note: what this limits: the mobility figures as a property of the material: they were PROBABLY STILL LIMITED BY DEFECTS IN PA[rent graphite], so they bound the sample rather than the substance
span.quote: From the linear dependence σ(Vg) we found carrier mobilities µ =σ/ne, which reached up to 5,000 cm2/Vs for both electrons and holes, were independent of temperature T between 10 and 100K and probably still limited by defects in parent graphite.

span.label: The measured minimum conductivity disagrees with the value most existing theories predict.
span.note: what this limits: the minimum-conductivity result against theory: THERE IS A BROAD THEORETICAL CONSENSUS THAT A 2D GAS OF DIRAC FERMIONS SHOULD EXHIBIT A MINIMUM CONDUCTIVITY OF ABOUT e2/h ... AND MOST THEORIES SUGGEST A VAL[ue] that the measurement does not match
span.quote: Although there is a broad theoretical consensus [18-23,10,11] that a 2D gas of Dirac fermions should exhibit a minimum 3 conductivity of about e2/h, this quantization was not expected to be accurate and most theories suggest a value of ≈e2/πh, in disagreement with the experiment.

span.label: The description that names the paper stops applying at two layers, and the authors say where.
span.note: what this limits: the massless Dirac description used here: the authors state that in two-layer graphene the fermions exhibit a finite mass and can no longer be described as massless Dirac particles
span.quote: fermions in the latter exhibit a finite mass near n ≈0 (as found experimentally; to be published elsewhere) and can no longer be described as massless Dirac particles

span.label: The explanation offered for the anomalous conductivity is qualitative and rests on an assumption the paper flags as an assumption.
span.note: what this limits: the account given here of the minimum conductivity: it is explained qualitatively, assuming the absence of localization, by invoking Mott's argument that the mean free path can never be shorter than the carrier wavelength
span.quote: Assuming the absence of localization, the observed minimum conductivity can be explained qualitatively by invoking Mott’s argument [21] that mean-free-path l of charge carriers in a metal can never be shorter that their wavelength

span.label: The theoretical prediction of the effect arrived from groups who did not know the experiment existed.
span.note: what this limits: the agreement between this measurement and theory: the half-integer QHE was suggested by two theory groups stimulated by the authors' earlier work on thin graphite films but unaware of the present experiment
span.quote: The half-integer QHE in graphene has recently been suggested by two theory groups [10,11], stimulated by our work on thin graphite films [2] but unaware of the present experiment

span.label: graphene charge carriers behave as massless Dirac fermions, letting a condensed-matter experiment probe relativistic QED and cosmology-relevant physics
span.quote: the subtle and rich physics of quantum electrodynamics

span.label: Dirac fermion
span.quote: The effect is single-particle and intimately related to subtle properties of massless Dirac fermions, in particular, to the existence of both electron- and hole-like Landau states at exactly zero energy

span.label: rest mass
span.quote: implies zero rest mass

span.label: cyclotron mass
span.quote: implies zero rest mass, their cyclotron mass is not zero

span.label: pseudospin
span.quote: The latter have nothing to do with the real spin but are “built in” the Dirac-like spectrum of graphene, and their origin can be traced to the presence of two carbon sublattices

span.label: Dirac equation
span.quote: Here we report a condensed matter system where electron transport is essentially governed by the Dirac equation and charge carriers mimic relativistic particles with zero mass

span.label: mass - TWO MASSES, ONE ZERO AND ONE NOT, IN THE SAME PARTICLE: the linear spectrum implies zero rest mass while the cyclotron mass is explicitly not zero, so a tag reading 'mass = 0' and one reading 'mass is not 0' are both correct here and neither is usable without saying which mass
span.quote: implies zero rest mass, their cyclotron mass is not zero

span.label: the plus-or-minus sign - SPINS IN QED, PSEUDOSPINS IN GRAPHENE: the authors carry a formula across from quantum electrodynamics and then state that the quantity it indexes here has nothing to do with real spin, its origin being the two carbon sublattices
span.quote: The latter have nothing to do with the real spin but are “built in” the Dirac-like spectrum of graphene, and their origin can be traced to the presence of two carbon sublattices

span.label: Dirac fermion - BY MIMICRY, NOT BY IDENTITY: the charge carriers are said to MIMIC relativistic particles with zero mass, under a Dirac equation borrowed from relativistic physics, with an effective speed of light the paper itself puts in scare quotes
span.quote: Here we report a condensed matter system where electron transport is essentially governed by the Dirac equation and charge carriers mimic relativistic particles with zero mass

span.label: builds-on → the Dirac equation (relativistic quantum mechanics / particle physics)
span.quote: electron transport is essentially governed by the Dirac equation

span.label: builds-on → Mott's argument on the minimum mean free path in a metal
span.quote: Assuming the absence of localization, the observed minimum conductivity can be explained qualitatively by invoking Mott’s argument [21] that mean-free-path l of charge carriers in a metal can never be shorter that their wavelength λF.

span.label: builds-on → the Atiyah-Singer index theorem
span.quote: The latter can be viewed as a direct consequence of the Atiyah-Singer index theorem that plays an important role in quantum field theory and the theory of superstrings [13,14].

span.label: builds-on → Berry's phase
span.quote: Note however that from another perspective the phase shift can be viewed as the direct manifestation of Berry’s phase acquired by Dirac fermions moving in magnetic field [15,16].

span.label: rest mass —distinct-from→ cyclotron mass
span.quote: implies zero rest mass, their cyclotron mass is not zero

span.label: Dirac fermion —operationalised-as→ Dirac equation
span.quote: Here we report a condensed matter system where electron transport is essentially governed by the Dirac equation and charge carriers mimic relativistic particles with zero mass

span.label: c* ≈ 10^6 m/s — effective speed of light of massless charge carriers in graphene
span.quote: charge carriers mimic relativistic particles with zero mass and an effective “speed of light” c∗ ≈106m/s

span.label: half-integer — anomalous filling factors of the graphene quantum Hall effect
span.quote: the integer quantum Hall effect in graphene is anomalous in that it occurs at halfinteger filling factors

span.label: π — Berry phase shift exhibited by the Dirac fermions
span.quote: exhibit a phase shift of π due to Berry’s phase

span.label: In graphene, electron transport is governed by the DIRAC equation: charge carriers behave as massless relativistic particles with effective speed c*≈10^6 m/s — a 2D gas of Dirac fermions.
span.quote: electron transport is essentially governed by the Dirac equation and charge carriers mimic relativistic particles with zero mass and an effective “speed of light” c∗ ≈106m/s

span.label: This yields unusual phenomena: an anomalous half-integer quantum Hall effect, a nonzero minimum conductivity, and a Berry-phase π shift.
span.quote: the integer quantum Hall effect in graphene is anomalous in that it occurs at halfinteger filling factors; b) graphene’s conductivity never falls below a minimum value

span.label: electron/hole concentration (gate voltage)
span.quote: Hall conductivity σxy of graphene plotted as a function of electron and hole concentrations

span.label: quantum Hall conductivity (plateaux)
span.quote: the plateaux correspond to half-integer ν so that the first plateau occurs at 2e2/h
